qs.q: Central diabetes insipidus is confirmed by which pattern?
o: Low urine osmolality (<300) + high serum osmolality/Na → corrects with DDAVP
Concentrated urine corrected by water deprivation only
Normal serum osmolality with dilute urine
High urine osmolality, low plasma Na
qs.e: Central DI is due to ADH deficiency, leading to the inability to concentrate urine despite high serum osmolality. Water deprivation fails to increase urine osmolality, but administration of DDAVP (a synthetic ADH analog) causes significant urine concentration. This distinguishes it from nephrogenic DI.
qs.s: Chemical Pathology — MCQ Bank — Cardiovascular System Pathology

qs.q: Central diabetes insipidus is distinguished from nephrogenic DI by
qs.e: Water deprivation then desmopressin: central DI responds (urine concentrates). Nephrogenic DI = no response (renal resistance to ADH).
